publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: In the new era of electric vehicles, battery swapping technology becomes a new trend except in plug in and hybrid vehicles. The awareness among the end user on battery handling becomes so vital. From the surveys carried out and studies on battery handling, many factors lead to battery blast, one among them is the external factors. In this paper external factors that affect the battery health such as temperature, humidity and vibration have been taken into account for monitoring and analysis by placing the system set up on a lithium ion battery. The influence of the aforementioned external factor has been studied in view with battery swapping that involves detecting the SoC and deducing equivalent pay from the users' wallet. A prototype model has been built and the results are analyzed and validated.

articleTitle: Single Switch High Gain Converter for Pulsed Electric Field
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: Most individuals prefer utilizing conventional methods like heating, cooking, freezing, chilling, and blanching for home meal preparation. However, in a broader context, food processing companies integrate these techniques with diverse technical approaches that are seldom utilized by consumers for home processing. Contemporary technologies encompass extrusion, microwave processing, high-pressure vacuum heating, and rapid high-temperature heating, which are less common in household food preparation. These methods prioritize the preservation of food quality in food preservation practices. Consequently, researchers are increasingly intrigued by non-thermal food processing methods as alternatives to conventional thermal techniques. Pulsed electric field (PEF) technology the least heat intensive non-thermal method facilitates lower processes temperatures effective energy utilize and the retention of quality rich food attributes encompassing nutrients with good flavour, color, and taste. Additionally, to facilitate PEF food processing, a pulsed voltage generator is imperative. It is imperative to assess the ripple voltage of each single-switch converter in comparison to others. The ripple voltage disparity between converters is pronounced, with one exhibiting notably higher levels than the other. To address this issue and enhance its applicability for Pulsed Electric Field (PEF) applications, modifications will be applied to a switching inductor. These alterations aim to markedly diminish the ripple voltage, rendering it more appropriate for PEF applications.

articleTitle: Urban Slum Mapping Using Homogeneous Urban Patches
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: Slums (Informal Settlements) are the most dynamic areas whose geographical locations are inaccurate according to official statistics and maps because of the exponential expansion of urbanization strategies. As a result, a method has to be developed to distinguish between informal settlements and track their spatial patterns. This paper presents an integrated method for detecting slums from satellite images that employs homogeneous urban patches (HUP) and grey level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM)-based image segmentation. In order to extract meaningful spatial features, urban patches are segmented according to their homogeneity and GLCM analysis provides useful texture information about slum areas. The combination of both these GLCM and HUP features allows for the creation of a classification map that accurately identifies and maps slum areas. We utilized WorldView-2 (1.84m) satellite imagery of Madurai to test the effectiveness of proposed HUP approach. The validation process includes rigorous testing against ground truth data, with careful consideration given to the selection of training and testing datasets. The effectiveness of the proposed method is evaluated using metrics including overall accuracy, user accuracy, and producer accuracy Furthermore, the proposed algorithm outperformed existing GLCM-based approaches in terms of accuracy.

articleTitle: Recognition of Type of Faults in Power Transformer Using Dissolved Gas Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: This paper discusses dissolved gas analysis (DGA) methods, which involve the Duval Triangle Method (DTM), Duval Pentagon Method (DPM), Heptagon Graph Method (HGM), and ratio methods, such as the IEC, Rogers, and Doernenburg method, for identifying issues in power transformers through process. A particular method to recognize the type of issue in a power transformer DGA is the Duval triangle. The fault zone is indicated, and its position in a triangle with equal sides is depicted using the proportionate quantities of three fault gases. The most accurate method of evaluating the condition of a power transformer has been shown to be DGA. Six distinct kinds of DGA power transformer problems can be identified using the DPM, a DGA graphical interpretation technique. They provide a review of the advantages and disadvantages of each plan, which may help decide the DGA method that will finish the test analysis most effectively. It averts further harm to that particular transformer by eliminating early transformer breakdowns. Lastly, the results of the study and future studies will be discussed.

articleTitle: Design of Two Stage Miller Compensated CMOS Opamp with Nulling Resistor in 90nm Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: Operational amplifier is considered to be the fundamental block mixed signal and analog design. This paper aims to design a two stage CMOS operational amplifier using Miller Compensation technique with a nulling resistor, mainly to achieve high gain with relatively good bandwidth and phase margin with low bias currents in 90 nm technology. Keeping this as a main aspect, Opamp specifications are taken into account, i.e., Differential Mode gain, common mode gain, phase margin, slew rate, power dissipation and gain bandwidth. This design operates at 1.2V to 0V half voltage supply swing. The simulation process is carried out in Cadence Virtuoso in 90nm node technology. The obtained DC gain is 68db with phase margin of 80 degree and a slew rate of 9 V/µSec with a power dissipation of 33µW.

articleTitle: Advancements in Plant Leaf Disease Classification: Integrating Machine Learning and Graph Convolutional Networks for Sustainable Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: In order to support life on Earth and preserve ecological equilibrium, plants are essential. However, a variety of biotic and abiotic elements constantly pose a threat to them; plant leaves are especially susceptible to illness. The ethology of plant leaf diseases, their consequences on plant health, and mitigation strategies are mined in this research. The categorization of plant leaf diseases both infectious and noninfectious the main topic of discussion. These illnesses threaten global foo d security and ecosystems because of their sensitivity to infections, the environment, and genetics. The significance of effective disease management is emphasized in the article, which takes into account elements like sustainable practices, data driven disease forecasting, and precision agriculture. The application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) is touted as a potent technique for classifying plant leaf diseases. The proposed approach, which makes use of graph convolutional networks, offers a fresh way to get around current problems. The importance of high-quality datasets for creating precise decision support systems is covered in the study. It is emphasized how adaptable ML models are, enabling ongoing learning and the identification of novel illnesses. Notwithstanding the progress made, obstacles including class imbalance and massive data problems are recognized, highlighting the necessity of meticulous experimental planning and model training.

articleTitle: Eagle Strategy based Improved Adaptive Control System for an Inverted Pendulum - Mobile Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: Navigation robot is required in industries to perform the assigned task. Therefore the robot should choose the shortest path to reach the given target. The computation time and cost should be less while making the decision. This work explains the position balancing of the Two Wheel Inverted Pendulum-Mobile Robot (TWIP-MR) system using the nature-inspired algorithm Eagle Strategy with Particle Swarm Optimization (ESPSO). According to stability concerns, this is an unstable open loop system exhibiting nonlinear behavior. The design of the system focuses on the balanced movement of the robot while moving towards the intended position. Two loops are offered while designing TWIP-MR, one for balancing the linear displacement and the other for maintaining the appropriate angular movement. This research uses a mathematical technique to provide an analysis of the TWIP-MR system. The random global search, intensive local search and a levy walk is adopted from Eagle search strategy. Particle Swarm Optimization is included in the local search stage of the ES. The PID controller is used in order to reduce the positional errors.

articleTitle: Autonomous Subsurface Exploration and Extraction System: Robotic Arm-Assisted Borewell Rescue Initiative
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: This groundbreaking hardware project introduces an advanced solution for borewell rescue operations, featuring a versatile robotic arm integrated with a robotic hook, vacuum pump, and precision control systems (powered by Raspberry Pi or Arduino). Employing Lidar sensors for real-time data acquisition, the system generates 3D models of the borewell environment, enhancing operational precision. The robotic arm, equipped with a hook for secure retrieval and a vacuum pump for debris removal, is seamlessly controlled for optimal coordination. Gas detectors ensure continuous monitoring of the borewell environment, prioritizing the safety of individuals within. The rescue mechanism involves a cable-manipulated container or steel rod, providing a controlled and reliable retrieval process. This project addresses the critical need for technological advancements in borewell rescues, offering an automated solution that boosts the safety and efficiency of rescue teams. Lidar sensors and advanced control systems add an intelligent layer, enabling real-time decision-making based on dynamic borewell conditions.

articleTitle: ANN Based Solar Panel Tracking with DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: Growth in renewable energy sources has generally increased due to the rising costs of fossil fuels and C02 emissions. To cope with consumer demands, more focus is being placed on renewable resources because of an increasing need for electricity. The production of power is heavily reliant on non-conventional sources. Due to its clean, inexhaustible, and environmentally friendly nature, solar energy has emerged as one of the leading renewable energy sources. Nevertheless, no end user load can be supported by the solar PV cell's fluctuating voltage. To control and enhance the voltage at the output terminal of the PV panel, choppers must be used. In this paper, a comparison of various MPPT algorithms is suggested to get the most output possible from the solar panel. Using a chopper, the proposed Artificial Neural Network (ANN) method is modeled and executed. In MATLAB/SIMULINK, a simulation analysis of the suggested PV -powered power electronic converter is conducted, and results are presented.

articleTitle: Modeling, Simulation, Time Response and Stability Analysis of Fuel Cell Based DC-DC Converter for EV Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: The paper presents the work carried out in Hydrogen fuel cell to sources the stabilized voltage. The work involves modeling the fuel cell, conventional boost converter, SEPIC converter and interleaved converter. A comparative analysis is made for the above three converters for different load changes. system involves Hydrogen Fuel Cell, DC-DC converter, and load. The simulation is carried out with Hydrogen fuel cell as source and the output voltage response is stabilized for different load conditions. It also includes the time response behavior and stability analysis of three converter topologies. The most suitable converter topology is identified from results for the Electric Vehicle (EV) application.

articleTitle: Gender Based Analysis of Insulin Like Growth Factor-1 (IFG-1) and Prevalence of Osteoporosis in South Indian Population
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: IGF-1 plays a pivotal role in promoting cell proliferation and growth, making it a key factor in growth-related diseases such as osteoporosis and diabetes. Serum IGF-1 levels can contribute to abnormal growth patterns, underscoring its significance in the pathophysiology of these conditions. Gender-based IGF-1 analysis is crucial for understanding and addressing variations in insulin-like growth factor-1 levels between men and women, providing valuable insights into potential gender-specific health implications and optimizing personalized healthcare interventions. The present study focuses gender based analysis in south Indian population because race is also one of the important factor in IGF 1 level. In this study, 195 blood samples have been collected from male and female volunteers and their IGF 1 value were quantified using systematic biochemical procedure with the help of ELIZA reader. Age-related analysis showed that IGF levels decrease with older age in both men and women. Women have significantly lower IGF 1 levels than men <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{p} < \mathbf{0.05})$</tex>. Especially during menopause, the IGF-1 levels of women decrease significantly. The bone mineral density T-score is low and showed greater correlation with IGF-1 level in female than male, which may be the reason for the high incidence of osteoporosis in women. However, further studies with different severities of osteoporosis are needed.

articleTitle: Predicting and Analyzing Student Exam Behavior with Distributed Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: Examinations are pivotal milestones in educational settings, serving not just as a measure of academic performance but also as a complex behavioral phenomenon. While traditional studies have explored student behaviors during examinations, the intricate, high-dimensional nature of such behaviors often escapes conventional analytical approaches. This paper introduces a novel methodology that employs Distributed Machine Learning techniques to analyze student behavior during exams compre- hensively. We design a system architecture that captures various behavioral metrics, and apply distributed machine learning algorithms to dissect this multi-faceted data. The findings offer actionable insights into optimizing examination processes and provide a pioneering framework for leveraging advanced com- putational techniques in educational psychology. Our empirical results demonstrate a substantial improvement in understanding student behaviors, potentially influencing educational policies and pedagogical strategies.

articleTitle: Producing Electricity from Discarded Plastic
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: Everything in the current situation is computerized. As a result, energy use has grown. Yet, a scarcity of natural resources has reduced the amount of power produced. We must use as much electricity as we can achieve it. Here, a heating panel is being used to generate electricity via waste management. Industrial processes produce trash that is not put to any useful use, is lost, discarded, or discharged into the environment. Several waste heat recovery systems can be used to recover the waste material, generating valuable energy sources while lowering overall energy usage. This paper goes into great detail into the operation of the system and the elements that went into its creation. It also discusses the theory underlying the system's operation and the viability of putting this concept into practice in third-world nations. It is revolutionary what this developing technology can do for the third-world nations. It involves renewing and reusing used energy to create more electric power than we can produce. This study discusses the potential applications of this design for industrial use as well as the possibility of storing the electrical energy produced by the wasted heat to make the device portable.

articleTitle: Early Prediction and Grading of Diabetic Retinopathy using Fusion Based Learning System
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR), a visual impairment caused by long-term diabetes mellitus, is a type of diabetes that destroys the retinal blood vessels. Determining and quantifying this form of diabetes from retinal pictures takes time and experience. The classification of DR necessitates the grading of multiple aspects. Finding the severity is a process that ophthalmologists must perform with great care and attention, and it may be error-prone. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with a transfer learning technique have been proposed to automatically diagnose diabetic retinopathy by gauging its severity. The enhanced version of VGG16 performed in a very admirable way. The rate of training and validation accuracy increased steadily with each subsequent frame. Overall, a VGG-16 model trained on the DIARETDB1 dataset achieved strong performance of 0.89 quadratic weighted kappa on the task of detecting diabetic retinopathy from fundus images. This suggests the approach is effective for this medical imaging application.

articleTitle: Performance and Analysis of Skin Cancer Detection Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: Skin cancer is notably one of the most dangerous expressions of this ailment, originating from DNA damage in skin cells that results in the formation of genetic abnormalities or mutations on the skin. The insidious characteristic of skin cancer lies in its inclination to gradually spread to other parts of the body, underscoring the importance of early detection for successful treatment. Given the increasing prevalence of skin cancer, its elevated mortality rate, and the significant expenses associated with medical interventions, prompt diagnosis becomes imperative. Acknowledging the severity of these challenges, researchers have developed various methods for the early identification of skin cancer. Parameters such as the symmetry, color, size, and shape of lesions are utilized to distinguish skin cancer and differentiate benign cases from melanoma. This paper explores deep learning approaches applied to the early detection of skin cancer, presenting the study's findings through tools, graphs, tables, techniques, and frameworks. This enhances comprehension and contributes to the body of knowledge in this critical field.

articleTitle: Power Enhancement Under Partial Shading Conditions Using Snake Moving Pattern Reconfiguration Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: Clean energy comes from solar power, which doesn't pollute the environment. Photovoltaic systems will be essential to the world's power production in the future. Partial shading is the most important consideration when installing PV plants in buildings. Partial shading is one of the drawbacks that reduce the performance of solar PV systems. In solar PV systems with partial shading, the amount of sunlight that reaches the shaded sections is reduced. This results in mismatch losses and lower total energy production. The mismatch loss can be mitigated by reconfiguration techniques or algorithms that dynamically modify the operation of solar PV modules to reduce the effect of shading and improve overall system performance. This work suggests a novel method for resolving the issue of partial shading while also increasing the PV array's overall power output. In this work, the Snake Moving Pattern array configuration method improves energy conversion in solar PV systems when there is partial shading. By arranging PV modules optimally when there is shading, this creative method seeks to increase performance. For improved shade dispersion, a 4 × 4 PV array uses a novel array configuration. MATLAB/Simulink® simulates the combination of the new array configuration and reconfiguration methods. The outputs are measured under every shading pattern and compared to the results of conventional methods. These simulations confirmed the superior performance of the proposed reconfiguration techniques in mitigating shading effects, outperforming existing methods. The suggested method is evaluated in a 4 × 4 Total Cross Tied (TCT) photovoltaic array with a 10W rating for each panel. In the 160W, 4 × 4 PV array test system, the suggested system's performance is examined in a range of partial shade scenarios.

articleTitle: Automated Guided Vehicle in an Industrial Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: The logistics of equipment and production-related items play a vital role in industrial production. Various movement scenarios are possible, including the transfer of logistics from the warehouse to the workspace, between workspaces, and from workspaces to dispatch. Automating these activities using Automated Guided Vehicles (AGVs) can streamline workflow. This paper proposes an AGV setup on the work floor for logistic applications. The AGV navigates the work floor using a line- following approach. Workers can raise requests from their specific workplaces, which are then prioritized. A central server monitors these requests and calculates the shortest path using the Dijkstra algorithm, transmitting it to the AGV. The server can also track the real-time location of the AGV. In cases of high-priority requests, the server estimates a new path based on the AGV's current location, allowing the AGV to efficiently handle high- priority tasks while robustly managing other tasks for a seamless production process.

articleTitle: Investigating the Effect of Shade on Rooftops Solar PV Systems in Hot Arid Regions
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: Rooftop solar photovoltaic (PV) systems offer distributed electricity generation options that effectively fulfill the energy requirements of a building. The primary difficulty associated with PV systems is their inherent variability, which is contingent upon ambient conditions. The photovoltaic characteristic varies in response to changes in temperature and irradiance conditions. For high-power applications, it is essential to use photovoltaic arrays instead of modules. Large photovoltaic (PV) systems may experience partial shading due to the presence of nearby buildings, trees, and the array itself. Partial shadowing refers to the situation where different modules within a photovoltaic (PV) array receive unequal levels of sun irradiation. This research specifically examines the modeling and analysis of rooftop solar photovoltaic (PV) systems in Bahrain, with a particular emphasis on the energy losses caused by shadowing in different climate conditions. The PV system simulation findings indicate that there is a decrease in energy production when the solar panels are exposed to shade.

articleTitle: Gesture-Controlled Wheelchair and Home Automation using IR Remote
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: Physically challenged people have discomfort in mobility due to several illness and issues. Improvisation in the lifestyle and quality of life for such individuals is the need of the society. The proposed study focuses on the mobility aid for the physically challenged individual by integrating an accelerometer sensor and an Arduino based controller allowing for the translation of natural hand gestures into precise motor commands in order to overrule the limitations of the traditional interfacing techniques fostering independence and social inclusivity for the estimated 75 million wheelchair users globally. The accelerometer sensor plays a pivotal role in tracking and interpreting the user's hand movements, creating a seamless interaction between human gestures and the motorized propulsion system of the wheelchair. The Arduino controller serves as the bridge, processing these gestures and orchestrating the corresponding movements, namely forward, backward, right, left and stop condition. A notable feature enhancing the wheelchair's usability is the incorporation of an infrared (IR)--based remote control system. This introduces a layer of home automation, enabling interaction with the surrounding environment using the same intuitive remote-control device. The gesture-controlled wheelchair seeks to empower users, providing not just a means of mobility but a tool for enhancing independence and confidence. Rigorous testing and evaluation protocols are integral to the development process, ensuring the accuracy of gesture recognition, responsiveness of motor control, and overall user experience.

articleTitle: Flood Survivor Detection through Image Fusion and Yolo Model
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: Natural disasters like flood happen when water overtakes normally dry places. During rescue missions aimed at saving lives, rescue teams responding to floods encounter numerous obstacles. Locating and discovering survivors is a vital component of rescue operations. For quick flood survivor recognition, the suggested approach combines image fusion with the YOLO (You Only Look Once) model, offering a novel method. This model utilizes image fusion by merging data from various sources, including RGB and Near Infrared Red (NIR) images captured by Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). In order to efficiently identify flood survivors and aid rescue crews in their effort to preserve lives, the resulting fused image is processed using the YOLO model.

articleTitle: Optimizing Battery Performance -Active and Passive Cell Balancing
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) are the transportation mode of the future. Due to their zero tailpipe emissions and minimal dependency on oil and its byproducts, EVs have gained popularity over the past ten years, with electric vehicle purchases increasing by 109% globally in 2021. Lithium-ion (Li-ion) battery packs are the primary energy source for the most recent completely electric vehicles, which has both benefits and drawbacks. Catastrophic casualties, such as poisonous smoke or fire, may result if the battery parameters are not maintained optimally in all circumstances. This paper's major goal is to show how to balance the voltages in each battery pack cell using a variety of cell balancing methods, such as active cell balancing and passive cell balancing. By preventing any cell from failing, this guarantees the battery pack's optimal performance. Active cell balancing is 23 percent more rapid compared to the results obtained from passive cell balancing.

articleTitle: Transmission Line Quality Inspection Using AI
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: This paper presents the application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques for quality inspection of transmission lines. Transmission lines play a crucial role in the reliable and efficient transfer of electrical power over long distances. However, faults and defects can occur due to various environmental and operational factors, leading to power outages and safety hazards. The proposed approach utilizes advanced Edge Deployable AI algorithms, including computer vision and Deep Learning, to automatically detect and classify potential faults and defects in transmission lines. The cutting edge high accuracy model is trained using i9 core, Nvidia RTX 3060 GPU with 6 GB vRAM, 16 GB RAM where we employ SSD - PyTorch based architecture and frameworks. The trained model is optimized to best accuracy and deployed over Nvidia Jetson Nano B01 using TensoRT Engine. A comprehensive dataset of images and videos of transmission lines is collected and labeled for training and testing the AI models. These models are trained to recognize patterns and anomalies indicative of various types of faults, such as broken conductors, insulator wear, and corrosion. The inspection process involves capturing images and videos of the transmission lines using drones or other surveillance systems. The captured data is then analyzed using the pre-trained AI models to identify potential issues. The AI algorithms can accurately detect and classify faults with high precision and recall, significantly reducing the need for manual inspection and minimizing human error. To enhance inspection accuracy, the AI models can be continuously updated and refined through a feedback loop using active learning algorithm.

Author Keywords: Nvidia Jetson Nano B01 using TensoRT Engine
Nvidia RTX 3060 GPU with 6 GB vRAM

articleTitle: Designing and Developing a Smart Wheelchair System using Raspberry Pi Comprising Hydrogel based Cushion and Pressure Mapping System to Prevent Decubitus Ulcers
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: Pressure ulcers, commonly known as bedsores, arise due to prolonged pressure on the skin, impacting both the epidermis and underlying tissues, typically occurring in bony areas of the body. With around 15% of the global population facing disabilities and a staggering 131.8 million individuals reliant on wheelchairs, addressing this health concern becomes paramount. A pioneering study presents an inventive approach to wheelchair design, specifically targeting the prevention of decubitus ulcers, prevalent and debilitating among wheelchair users. This system integrates cutting-edge technology and innovative materials, featuring a Raspberry Pi microcontroller and a revolutionary hydrogel-based cushion to proactively combat this condition. The cushion, a material science breakthrough, excels in pressure distribution and moisture management, significantly mitigating the risk of pressure sores for wheelchair users. Moreover, the system incorporates a pressure mapping system with advanced sensors for continuous monitoring of pressure points, providing essential feedback for optimized weight redistribution. The research explores inventive methods for adjusting seating positions to prevent decubitus and alleviate pressure points, working proactively to prevent ulcers. Additionally, an obstacle detection program enhances mobility solutions for wheelchair users, ensuring unparalleled comfort and actively preventing the development of decubitus ulcers.

articleTitle: Enhancing Protein Structure Generation Through Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: Protein structure prediction is a critical task in molecular biology, with far-reaching implications for innovation, disease understanding, and drug discovery. Deep learning is one successful way to deal with this difficult issue. The purpose of this work is to investigate how deep learning technologies can be used to increase the precision and effectiveness of protein structure formation. We examine numerous deep learning models and approaches in depth, emphasizing their advantages and disadvantages in terms of protein structure prediction. Our study includes a comparison of current deep learning-based approaches, demonstrating their usefulness on both benchmark datasets and real-world examples. We discuss how deep learning models are built by using inter-residue interactions, secondary structure prediction, and sequence data. In addition, we investigate how generative adversarial GANs could be utilized to improve protein structure formation by using complex data distributions. We show how deep learning may dramatically improve the precision of protein structure prediction, ultimately producing more dependable models, through extensive experiments and case studies. In addition, we discuss how deep learning models may be interpreted and applied to the field of protein folding, providing an understanding of both their strengths and weaknesses.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study on Machine Learning Models for a Crop Recommendation System
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: Agriculture contributes significantly in shaping the GDP of a nation. Farming is a crucial aspect in agricultural nations such as that of India. While numerous technological innovations have emerged in agriculture, the current need of the hour is the continual enhancement and improvement of the current technology at hand. Due to the diverse climatic conditions, an efficient technique becomes crucial for enabling better crop cultivation and supporting farmers in their production and management. Offering a recommendation system to farmers based on historic data can significantly assist in their crop cultivation. In this paper, analysis of crop dataset and crop recommendation is done using a variety of Machine Learning algorithms. The models used include traditional models such as Decision Tree Classifier, k-Nearest Neighbor and Naïve-Bayes Classifier. Ensemble Learning models such as Random Forest Classifier, a deep learning model, Multi-layer Perceptron Classifier as well as a hybrid model which combines the Decision Tree Classifier, Random Forest Classifier, Naïve-Bayes Classifier, Multi-Layer Perceptron Classifier and a Support Vector Classifier are also utilized in this paper. The models are evaluated, and their performance are assessed based on various evaluation metrics. The evaluation metrics include accuracy, precision, and recall, and F1 score of the models.

articleTitle: Prediction Of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: This is to investigate the predictive potential of electroencephalogram (EEG) signals extracted from children diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). The objective is to utilize machine learning techniques, specifically logistic regression, to discern patterns within EEG data that could aid in the early prediction of ASD. EEG signals collected from autism-affected children are analyzed and processed to extract relevant features. Subsequently, these features are used as inputs to train a logistic regression model. Thestudy evaluates the model's performance in distinguishing between ASD and typically developing individuals, aiming to provide a reliable predictive toolfor identifying ASD based on EEG signals. Results suggest promising prospects for leveraging EEG data and machine learning methods in the early detection and potential prediction of autism spectrum disorder in children.

articleTitle: Smart Forest Rover: Integrating Sensors, Cameras, and GPS for Environmental Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: This project introduces a significant enhancement to the Rocker-Bogie system. By integrating advanced sensors, including day and night vision cameras, temperature and humidity sensors, and GPS technology, our innovative “Smart Forest Rover” enables real-time data collection and analysis. This breakthrough promises to revolutionise forest conservation and research efforts by providing comprehensive, timely insights into these vital ecosystems. The Smart Forest Rover serves as a testament the power of technology in fostering a deeper understanding of our natural world and underscores its pivotal role in promoting sustainable conservation practices for the benefit of present and future generations.

articleTitle: A Filter Bank Multi-Carrier (FBMC) System with Multi-Carrier CDMA
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: FBMC displays superior spectral qualities when compared to OFDM. This research introduces an FBMC setup incorporating Multi- Carrier Code Division Multiple Access (MC- CDMA) to minimize both the Bit Error Rate (BER and Peak-to-Average Power Ratio (PAPR), thereby boosting overall system efficiency. Initially the input signal undergoes a spreading procedure to translate it into codes, subsequently transmitted through the channel using the O-QAM modulation scheme. Upon reception, these transmitted codes undergo demodulation and de-spreading. Initially deployed in a Single Carrier (SC) system, FBMC with CDMA is later expanded to a Multi-Carrier (MC) system. An assessment of BER performance was carried out for FBMC without signal spreading and FBMC with CDMA. This evaluation entailed BER calculations across various Signal-to-Noise Ratios (SNR), revealing a decrease in BER in comparison to FBMC without spreading. This decrease was consistent across the range of tested SNR values, illustrating the effectiveness of integrating CDMA in enhancing the FBMC system's performance.

articleTitle: Automatic Saline Reversal Control System using IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: In this study introduces an innovative Internet of Things (IoT)-based alert system designed for medical settings, with the primary goal of preventing saline reversal incidents. The administration of saline is crucial for patient recovery in healthcare facilities, but lapses in staff attention can lead to dangerous reversals. Our proposed system strategically places sensors in the saline network to detect improper flow, specifically backflow of blood, and promptly notifies medical staff via mobile message upon detection. If saline levels drop below a predefined limit, the sensor stops the flow and sends an alert. A user-friendly web application allows real-time monitoring of flow rates. The core components of the system include the ESP8266 as the master controller, a load cell for precise bottle weight measurement, and a servo motor for drip control. Efficient alerts are sent through the IFTTT server, ensuring timely communication via SMS or call. This technological innovation significantly enhances patient safety by reducing harmful incidents associated with saline administration. The web app provides healthcare staff with a convenient platform to monitor current saline levels, marking a critical advancement in healthcare technology for improved patient care and safety.

articleTitle: Neuro Computing-Based Models of Digital Marketing as a Business Strategy for Bangalore's Startup Founders
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: Large amounts of data are perfect for artificial intelligence. Women are more suited to and capable of doing this activity than males are. The use of AI in digital marketing is rapidly expanding. Predicting user behaviour, search cycles, and other aspects of digital marketing will be lot simpler with the aid of artificial intelligence. Perhaps this will enhance the efficiency of business websites. Using AI, companies may streamline their content creation processes. The actual world may be impacted by corporate marketing. Innovative methods of attracting and maintaining valuable customers via the pooling of resources, the management of digital risks, and the production of new value are the engines that power entrepreneurial marketing. These techniques form the backbone of the value creation process. A semi-structured questionnaire was sent to the proprietors of 272 newly established firms in Bangalore for the purpose of this research. The critical aspects of digital marketing were discovered using a two-layer 6-3-1 neural network model with hyperbolic tangent-purelin topology. Some of these components include being proactive; taking risks; using resources; concentrating on opportunities; increasing efforts; and producing value. The results might be useful for entrepreneurs in Bangalore that are looking to improve their digital marketing strategies.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Search and Rescue Bot
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: Recent advancements in Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) have transformed them into viable platforms for carrying sensors and computer systems capable of executing complex tasks. This research presents a method for implementing imaging and object recognition on standard hardware within an autonomous UAV to detect humans at a high frame rate in outdoor settings. By geo-locating these detected human positions, a map highlighting various points of interest can be generated. This saliency map can be invaluable in scenarios such as disaster relief operations, where it can assist in scheduling the delivery of medical supplies. The methodology has been successfully deployed and tested on the UAV Tech autonomous unmanned helicopter platform as part of a complete autonomous mission. This platform demonstrates stable flight characteristics and can effectively monitor and collect data in diverse regions. UAVs are increasingly utilized in hazardous environments, offering access to areas that are otherwise unreachable, facilitating tasks with remarkable ease. One of the primary applications of drones is in detecting human presence in areas affected by natural disasters, signaling nearby rescue teams via GSM technology. The outcomes of this study have enhanced the performance of this technique and have addressed its limitations

articleTitle: Design of PnR Flow For Block Level Chip for Optimizing Leakage Power
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: To satisfy the future requirements of chip design, modifications must be made to software/hardware capabilities, design tools, and procedures. Engineers developed an efficient structured ASIC chip architecture to make these changes while concentrating on the design characteristics. ASIC design cycle that is mature and silicon-tested consists of several stages, including designconception, leakage power optimization, logical/physicalimplementation, design validation, and design verification. In this project we figured out several techniques to optimize leakage power. That includes using of LVT, HVT and Multi-threshold voltage cells in the placement and routing stage. Later we observed that a significant figure of leakage power has been reduced i.e. from 6.29e+05 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> 5.39e+05 n W.

articleTitle: Varicose Vein Detection and Real-Time Integration using Faster R-CNN Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: Varicose veins are a prevalent vascular disorder affecting a significant portion of the population. This study aims to develop a user-friendly and cost-effective screening tool for early diagnosis and monitoring of varicose veins. A custom deep learning model was trained on a meticulously curated dataset of varicose vein images, categorizing them as “Normal” and “Varicose.” The model's effectiveness was validated using a comprehensive dataset divided into training, testing, and validation. The system also extends to realtime varicose vein detection through laptop cameras, providing instant visual feedback for timely intervention. This real-time capability is complemented by long-term monitoring, making it a valuable tool for both clinical and home-based use. The proposed solution aligns with modern healthcare requirements, enabling early intervention in varicose vein management and contributing to improved healthcare outcomes.

articleTitle: A Multi-Port High Gain DC-DC Boost Converter for Renewable Energy Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: One among the most crucial parts of green energy systems is thought to be high-gain DC/DC converters. Utilizing an excessive duty cycle, a great deal of high-gain converters are used to enhance the gain of voltage. However, it raises expenses and losses, deteriorates system performance, and results in low efficiency. Combining the good aspects of the high gain converter with a three-port converter is quite advantageous. A DC/DC boost converter that operates with a gain which is high will be discussed here. Applications requiring a high voltage gain and low input voltage, including fuel cell and solar photovoltaic systems, may find usage for this converter. The topology is distinguished by its ease of use, improved gain of voltage, improved efficiency, and continuity of the input current. To enhance system performance, the control logic also incorporates an energy management system. The control methods, which includes energy management and topology's viability was demonstrated using MATLAB/Simulink

articleTitle: Design of Intelligent Intrusion Detection System using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: An intrusion is any deliberate attempt to get through a network's defenses and make it less available, less private, or all three. Intrusions include anything from threats to break the rules for acceptable use to threats to break basic security rules. When an attacker gains access to a system through a trusted person or the internet of systems in order to gain more privileges and then use them in some way, this is called a breach. “Intrusion detection” is the process of checking to see if someone has tried to break security, privacy, or the availability of resources. This article presents development of intelligent intrusion detection system using machine learning. ACO is used for feature optimization and Support Vector machine, K-NN, and Naïve Bayes algorithm is used for classification.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of Passive Cell Balancing Schematic for Battery Module with Eight Cells
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: Since the battery is the most important component of an electric vehicle, it accounts for about 30-40% of the entire cost of the vehicle. The number of series and parallel connections between the battery's cells depends on parameters such as voltage and current. In nature, battery cells with identical ratings exhibit distinct tendencies because of variations in their internal structure and manufacturing processes. There is an imbalance in the cells as a result of the variations in cell behavior. We require balancing circuitry to use the cell's capacity fully. This work employs the passive cell balancing schematic to balance the voltages, currents, and states of charge of cells coupled as banks using a combination of parallel and series assembly. Obtaining equal voltages and state of charge for each of the module's cells indicates that the balancing process is complete.

articleTitle: Integrated Women's Security System with Safe Route Navigation and Instant Law Enforcement Reporting
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: Designed to empower women in many daily situations, the integrated women's safety app is a comprehensive smartphone software that tackles safety concerns. This program offers a complete safety solution by combining various features and technologies. Users may quickly notify approved emergency contacts of their whereabouts by using the app's built-in emergency response system. Furthermore, it integrates with the city government's emergency services, facilitating seamless collaboration during critical circumstances. Users can stay safer when doing things like late-night commuting or traveling alone thanks to the app's real-time GPS tracking, which they can then share with trusted friends. Additionally, there is a panic button on the app that, when pressed, instantly contacts emergency services. Effective crisis prevention and management is possible with the aid of the software's self-defense classes, safety guidance, information on nearby safe zones, and hotlines.

articleTitle: Augmented Fuzzy-ILC for Trajectory Tracking Control of Magnetic Levitation System
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: Magnetic levitation, which is also known as maglev, is a technology that uses a magnetic field to levitate an object and keep it suspended in mid-air. Maglev systems are unstable and nonlinear in an open loop, a controller is required to tackle the non-linearity present in the system. There are several controllers like PID (Proportional-Integral-Derivative), and PIV (Proportional plus Integral plus Velocity) have been proposed. ILC (Iterative Learning control) is a scheme that works to enhance the outcomes through information-based dynamics learning, whereas at every iteration, the PID controller generates the same tracking error and adjusts control signal according to the time index. ILC augmented with PID Controller gives better tracking control. However, the tracking performance can be improved further by combining Fuzzy with ILC. Improved robustness and trajectory tracking of the maglev system can be attained by augmenting Fuzzy with ILC.

articleTitle: Tailored Deep Learning Approaches for Binary Classification and Evaluation of Diabetic Foot Ulcer Images
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: The frequent issue of blood glucose level that causes Diabetic Foot Ulcer (DFU) which is not properly controlled and diagnosed that leads to gangrene and amputation. To identify the early detection of diabetic foot ulcer promptly, we used deep learning approaches such as DenseNet121, CNN, VGG16, VGG19 and ResNet50 for the classification of normal and abnormal foot images. Evaluating various algorithms functionality and choosing the best structure to obtain precise DFU recognition. The dataset was preprocessed with pixel values being normalized and further rotation, shifts, zoom and various DL models were applied. To evaluate, the data set was classified into validation and training phases. Multiple convolutional, pooling layers, flatten, dense, dropout and ReLU architecture are used for binary classification of DFU pictures. Adam optimizer, Binary cross entropy and Loss Function were employed by the model. The experimental results demonstrated that Densenet121 achieved an outstanding accuracy of 99%. The model exhibits an impressive ability to differentiate between normal and abnormal DFU cases. It is evidenced by sensitivity-specificity calculations and the analysis of the confusion matrix. This study demonstrates the way deep-learning algorithms that categorize the DFU images and provide support models for healthcare professionals to accelerate the diagnosis of DFUs and to reduce the leg amputation and mortality rate.

articleTitle: IoT-Enhanced Hostel Inventory Management System for Seamless Resource Monitoring and Control
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: The Hostel Inventory Management System (HIMS) is a sophisticated solution designed to streamline and optimize inventory management in hostel facilities. It utilizes Internet of Things (IoT) technology, specifically Blynk and the ESP32 microcontroller, to automate and enhance the process. The system features a load cell with an amplifier, an LCD, and three micro switches for categorizing food items (dhal, rice, and wheat). The ESP32 microcontroller ensures seamless communication and coordination between components. The LCD provides real-time updates on inventory status, making it easy for users to access information. The system also has three micro switches that can differentiate food types, facilitating precise tracking and monitoring. The system also serves as an auditory alert system, notifying administrators or users of critical events or low inventory levels. Blynk, an IoT platform, enables remote monitoring and control of the HIMS. Users can access the system through a mobile application, providing real- time updates, notifications, and control over inventory-related activities. The proposed HIMS offers a comprehensive and efficient solution for hostel inventory

articleTitle: OFDM based Waveform Design and Digital Beamforming Technique for RADCOM System
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: The utilization of orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) in wireless communication systems has become widely popular due to its effectiveness in mitigating frequency selective fading and enhancing spectral efficiency. This study introduces a RADCOM (Radar Communication) system utilizing OFDM, incorporating digital beamforming to enhance its performance. Through simulation results, the proposed system surpasses conventional OFDM-based RADCOM systems in terms of bit error rate (BER) and signalto-noise ratio (SNR) across various distances by amplifying the SNR of received signals. Moreover, it demonstrates superior resistance to multi-path fading and interference, suggesting its applicability in diverse RADCOM scenarios.

articleTitle: Sun Position Tracking of Solar Panel
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: The goal of this project is to use a servo motor to design and build a solar panel sun position tracking system. Because the solar panel is currently set in place, it is less effective at capturing solar energy. To solve this problem, a solar tracker is suggested, which uses a servo motor to modify the solar panel's position in response to the sun's varying positions during the day. By accurately tracking the sun's position extraction and improving the overall performance of the solar panel. Additionally, the system incorporates Light Dependent Resistor (LDR) sensors to detect the intensity of sunlight. These sensors provide real-time feedback on the brightness of the surrounding environment, allowing the solar tracker to make precise adjustments to the panel's position. By combining the servo motor's movement with the LDR sensor data, the system ensures that the solar panel maintains an optimal alignment with the sun's rays, maximizing the amount of solar energy captured. This integration of servo motors and LDR sensors results in an efficient and accurate sun-tracking system for enhanced solar power generation. The sun position tracking system uses LDR sensors to measure sunlight intensity and provide feedback. It Adjusts the solar panel's alignment, optimizing energy absorption. The system combines LDR sensors and servo motor control for efficient and automated sun tracking, Enhancing solar energy utilization [1], [13].

articleTitle: Image Processing based Animal Intrusion Detection System in Agricultural Field using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: Agriculture is one of the most important industries in any economy since it plays a big role in the food supply chain. Agricultural fields, on the other hand, confront a number of issues, including animal encroachment, which can cause severe crop damage and loss. Traditional animal control tactics, such as electrical fences, physical barriers, and scarecrows, can be inefficient, time-consuming and a serious threat to animal lives. The animals either become entangled in the fence's wire mesh or were electrocuted by the electric lines. To overcome these problems we propose a unique method that involves image processing-based animal incursion detection system in agricultural fields using Raspberry Pi and deep learning technique, mainly the YOLOv7. This technology captures live video feeds of agricultural fields using a camera and analyses them using deep learning algorithm to detect any animal invasions. If an intrusion is detected, the system emits specific repellent sounds for specific animal via speakers in order to scare them away and alerts the farmers by sending SMS. This method provides an efficient and practical alternative for crop damage prevention and human-wildlife conflict reduction in agricultural settings.

articleTitle: Relevant Musical Schema-based Human Emotion Controller using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: Musical Schema negotiation describes how a user's facial expressions may convey their emotional state or mood. You may see these expressions in the live video from the system camera. Many efforts are being made to teach machines to recognize various human emotions or moods in the field of computer vision and machine learning (ML). There are several techniques available in machine learning to identify human emotions. We propose a system that detects mood in real time and generates a mood-based music player that recommends songs depending on the observed mood. This is now a function that comes pre-installed on the traditional music player applications on our phones. One major benefit of mood detection integration is customer satisfaction. Among this system's objectives are to analyze the user's look, forecast their expression, and suggest music based on how they seem.

articleTitle: Leukemia Cancer Detection in Microscopic Blood Samples using Optimized Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: Leukaemia causes blood cell abnormalities quickly. Leukocytes injure bone marrow or blood and are followed by an increase in growing lymphocytes. Gelatinous tissue produces most of the body's blood. Thus, early and accurate cancer detection is essential for effective treatment that improves survival. Manually studying blood samples from microscopic pictures to identify this illness is slow, inaccurate, and timeconsuming. This sickness is currently diagnosed manually by studying blood samples from microscopic images, which is arduous, slow, and imprecise. Furthermore, leukemic cells appear and act similarly to normal cells under a microscope, making identification more challenging. Though DL has developed advanced algorithms for detecting difficulties in recent decades, there is always room for improvement in performance, learning process, and efficacy. A hybrid approach using parallel swarm optimisation is more successful for identifying WBC leukaemia. To obtain high accuracy in picture classification, convolutional network hyperparameter tweaking is critical, but it involves significant computing effort. An automated leukaemia monitoring system for small blood samples was created utilising metaheuristics and parallel cat swarm optimisation (PCSO) to determine optimum convolutional neural network settings. Two public leukaemia blood sample databases, ALL IDB1 and ALL IDB2, are utilised. The method's resilience and effectiveness are shown by experimental findings and comparison with other cutting-edge algorithms under similar conditions.

articleTitle: Unlocking the Potential of Virtual Pet Ownership - The Impact of Blockchain and Web3
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: Virtual pet ownership has witnessed significant advancements with the emergence of blockchain and Web3 technology. This research paper delves into the transformative impact of integrating blockchain in virtual pet platforms, focusing on the case study of Meta-Pet. Through a comprehensive literature review and critical analysis of 17 relevant papers, this study examines the potential of decentralized technology in redefining ownership, care, and trading mechanisms for digital pets. The methodology involves a detailed exploration of the implementation process, followed by a thorough analysis of the implications and challenges associated with the adoption of blockchain and Web3 in the Meta-Pet platform. The findings underscore the enhanced user engagement and the potential for fostering trust and transparency in virtual pet communities. The research highlights the significance of this integration and provides insights into the future-prospects of blockchain and Web3 in the virtual pet landscape.

articleTitle: Hybrid 9-Port Power Divider and Combiner for Enhanced Wireless Energy Harvesting in Passive RFID Tag Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: This research introduces innovative configurations for hybrid power divider combiners (HPDCs) featuring five and nine ports, aligning with the standards set by IEEE 802.11b, g, ISM, and 802.11. The HPDCs are designed to operate at multiple bands—2.45 GHz, 5.8 GHz, and 6 GHz— corresponding to IEEE 802.11n, a, and 802.11ac, respectively. These tailored designs are specifically crafted to address the energy-efficient requirements of applications spanning the DC to 6-GHz frequency range. Notable applications include 5Genabled Passive Internet of Things (IoT) sensors, Energy Harvesting (E.H) tags, and Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) antenna beamforming. When implemented on an FR4 substrate, the proposed HPDC configurations demonstrate consistent power distribution, robust port isolation, and excellent port matching, particularly at a central design frequency of 3 GHz. These designs hold great promise in the context of satellite-cellular convergence, finding potential applications in RF energy harvesting, adaptive intelligent energy-efficient data transmission, and seamless connectivity. Of significance is the achievement of return and isolation losses falling below −7 dB, meeting the criteria for Wi-Fi 6E. This underscores the suitability of the proposed HPDCs for advanced wireless applications, affirming their potential contribution to RF energy harvesting, adaptive data transmission, and enhanced connectivity within the specified frequency range.

articleTitle: An Examination of Machine Learning Applications in the Field of Cybersecurity Approaches for Detecting and Mitigating Threats
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: Assessing significant AI moves toward that are utilized for the recognition of critical digital dangers in the advanced climate is the reason for this exploration drive. A comprehensive examination concerning these strategies is remembered for the assessment. The examination will zero in on spam discovery, interruption recognition, and malware location, and it will utilize datasets that are consistently used as well as benchmark datasets. AI is turning into an undeniably significant part in the domain of network protection, which is generally a work in progress. The significant goal is to work on the most common way of recognizing malware by making it more noteworthy, adaptable, and fruitful in contrast with the ordinary methodologies that underscore human cooperation. The issues that AI brings to the field of network safety require the executives that is both thorough and hypothetical to be tended to. With regards to decreasing the impacts of cyberattacks, various AI and factual procedures, including AI, support vector machines, and Bayesian grouping, have demonstrated to be valuable. As a component of the most common way of planning keen security frameworks, it is important to uncover recently covered examples and experiences inside network information, and afterward to foster information driven AI models that are in accordance with these patterns. To guarantee the security of the framework, the review puts an accentuation on the utilization of AI methods to observation information. The present network protection chances are talked about, and the manners by which AI procedures are applied to battle these dangers are explored. The exploration additionally causes to notice the changing attack designs that have happened throughout the most recent decade and investigates the deficiencies of the latest models. As the danger presented by malware that objectives online networks keeps on raising, the design is to assess the adequacy of the various AI calculations that are right now accessible.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach to Educational Augmented Reality: Real-Time Enhancement and Interactivity
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: To improve the student's ability in recalling difficult concepts and materials, it is necessary to introduce a change in the education system. Augmented reality is a technology that is still developing. It is crucial to comprehend its development and the true impact it has on education. Exploring how to make use of augmented reality in the development of student-focused learning experiences is important. The AR Based Education System overcomes the problems in the conventional education system by developing an engaging and interactive study tool which aims in changing the education system. This AR Based Education System will provide a dynamic learning experience that combines different learning methods such as visualization, interactivity and flexibility. By letting students to learn as they see fit, it is ensured that they remain attentive throughout the learning process and facilitate a much simpler understanding of subjects. This demonstrates how much more efficient and enjoyable learning can be made.

articleTitle: Enhancing Storage Efficiency for Health Data Records through Block chain-Based Storj Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: Modern healthcare systems are complex, and patient information is frequently shared with doctors, patients, and shareholders. Traditional EHR methods were used to protect patient records, and these methods faced a few challenges related to compatibility, unintentional information disclosure, and invalid access. Recent healthcare systems that depend on digital health records entail systems that include integrity, security, and confidentiality of patient records. This paper proposes a blockchain technology, that is, the Storj mechanism, as a solution to the problems that were faced by the traditional methods. This method provides a decentralized, tamper-resistant, and transparent framework for storing and sharing medical data. The Storj mechanism complies with data protection regulations such as the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA). It provides a standardised platform and facilitates interoperability between different healthcare systems and institutions. The outcomes obtained using Storj's mechanism for managing medical health records include enhanced security, privacy, compliance, interoperability, efficiency, and facilitation of medical research.

articleTitle: Human-Robot Collaboration in the Workplace: Assessing the Impact on Employee Well-Being and Productivity
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: As the integration of robots into various industries becomes increasingly prevalent, understanding the nuanced effects on the workforce is imperative. This study investigates the implications of Human-Robot Collaboration (HRC) in the workplace, specifically focusing on its impact on employee well-being and productivity. Leveraging advanced deep learning methodologies, the proposed Long Short-Term Memory – Gated Recurrent Unit (LSTM-GRU) model is introduced as a novel approach for assessing these critical factors. Implemented in Python, the LSTM-GRU model serves as a powerful tool for assessing the multifaceted dynamics of HRC. The utilization of deep learning techniques, coupled with the LSTM-GRU architecture, allows for a more nuanced understanding of the intricate relationships between human and robotic collaborators in the workplace. The findings of this study contribute valuable insights for organizations seeking to optimize HRC integration, highlighting the significance of advanced computational approaches in gauging the impact on employee well-being and productivity. The Python implementation further enhances the model's accessibility, enabling researchers and practitioners to adopt and adapt this methodology in diverse workplace settings. The study employs a diverse set of performance metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-Score, to comprehensively evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed model. The results reveal a remarkable accuracy of 99.11% for the LSTM-GRU model, showcasing its superior ability to capture nuanced temporal dependencies in comparison to existing methods such as Convolutional Neural Network(CNN), CNN-LSTM, and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM). The proposed model's accuracy surpasses these methods by 3.23%, underscoring its robustness in accurately identifying and predicting aspects related to employee well-being and productivity.

Author Keywords: Long Short-Term Memory – Gated Recurrent Unit (LSTM-GRU)

articleTitle: Performance Indicators for the Robotics Engineering Operational Scheduling
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: This study examines multi-stage robotic production line performance via queuing analysis to enable more accurate resource planning. It is one of a select few studies of this type designed to boost the efficiency of manufacturing robots with many stages. The goal of this study is to assist managers in increasing productivity and effectiveness while choosing the best policy for assembly systems. The study utilizes an analytical methodology based on actual data from a firm that manufactures robots. The process of making a robot involves several different processes, including identifying the problem, researching and designing the solution, developing a prototype, building the robot, programming and testing the robot, and ultimately assessing the robot. The necessary information for each workstation was gathered, and the Supplementary Variable approach was used to ascertain the processing component arrival and departure distribution statistics. The queueing analysis presented in this work serves as a foundation for predicting and analyzing production systems using metrics like utilization, the proportion of idle workstations, the number of batches in the system, the number of batches in the queue, the expected time spent in the queue, and the expected time spent in the system.

articleTitle: Life Span Prediction of Lithium-Ion Battery Using Optimization Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: The process to determine the unknown parameters of a battery model using experimental data is known as parameter identification of lithium-ion batteries utilizing optimization techniques. This challenge is solved by using optimization techniques to identify the set of parameters that minimizes the error between the experimental data and the model output. When a lithium-ion battery is being parameter identified utilizing the Grey Wolf Algorithm (GWO). Specific goals of a lithium-ion battery parameter identification using the Grey Wolf Optimization Method include figuring out the parameters of a model that can be used to estimate the battery's voltage, current, state of charge (SOC), state of temperature (SOT), state of health (SOH), and remaining useful life (RUL). Identify the features that define the battery's ability to produce electricity at different discharge rates. The performance and lifespan of the battery are determined by these factors.

articleTitle: Design and Fabrication of Self-Propelled Fertilizer Spreader
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: In the Agriculture Sector, Precision farming techniques are undergoing a revolutionary change with the goal of maximizing resource efficiency and reducing environmental impact. This Research Paper examines about the viability and advantages of incorporating battery-operated systems into fertilizer spreaders for the further development of effective and sustainable farming methods. The study begins by reviewing the current state of fertilizer spreading technologies, emphasizing the importance of precision and uniformity in nutrient application. It then introduces the concept of battery-operated fertilizer spreaders as a potential solution to address the limitations of traditional, fossil fuel-dependent counter parts. Field tests are used in the study technique to compare traditional models versus battery-operated fertilizer spreaders in a range of crop and soil situations. Carefully examined and studied are parameters including application rates, spreading precision, and operating expenses. The research also evaluates the effect on the environment, taking into account elements like carbon emissions, soil health, and sustainability in general. The primary focus is on evaluating the performance, economic viability, and environmental implications of this emerging technology. The purpose of this research is to offer useful information to farmers, producers of agricultural equipment, and legislators who are looking for sustainable solutions for contemporary farming methods. The use of fertilizer spreaders powered by batteries has the potential to greatly enhance precision farming and promote a more ecologically responsible and sustainable method of managing crop nutrient levels.

articleTitle: Enhanced Deep Learning Techniques to Classify Tamil Handwritten Characters
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: Tamil handwritten document digitization is becoming increasingly dependent on exploit of handwritten character identification. Tamil is solitary of the mainly used traditional languages within India, especially in south. It can be exceedingly difficult to detect a non-digitized character because tamil has such a great and multipart character set. The Inception model and other convolution neural networks aid in classification of various type of objects on images. Here, symmetric and asymmetric structure blocks to facilitate the model itself include convolutions, average, max pooling, concatenations, dropouts, and completely linked layers. The batch normalization, which is used broadly in the model and is also functional to the inputs for activation of the function. SoftMax is used to compute loss. To differentiate handwritten characters for better classification, we employed Inception. In this article, we evaluate the handwritten character identification for tamil by means of ResNet, Inception v3, VGG16, and VGG19. There are 1609 test images and 3901 train images in the 156-class dataset.

articleTitle: Image Captioning based on Encoder Decoder Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: Images are essential for communicating ideas, feelings, and narratives in the era of digital media and content consumption. Computers to produce textual data for an image that replaces humans. Image captioning is a fascinating fusion of computer vision (CV) and Natural Language Processing (NLP) that aims to generate text from an image. By using these technologies, images can be used as an approachable, meaningful, and descriptive form of communication. Because of its wide range of uses, image captioning has attracted a lot of attention. Strong feature representations and context-aware language generation algorithms are necessary to overcome the major challenge of bridging the semantic gap between visuals and text.
